project.project_status_at_last_discussion: Client purchased GoDaddy hosting and developer was transitioning from Netlify to GoDaddy hosting
project.developer_experience: Second substantial web development project; strong CS background but limited formal web development experience

original_architecture.workflow: Generate/download website code, modify it with AI, deploy to Netlify, connect the GoDaddy domain

problem.issue: Developer could not properly configure the client's GoDaddy domain because the developer did not have access to the client's GoDaddy account
problem.authentication: GoDaddy account required 2FA through the client
problem.client_role: Very hands-off and gave developer significant freedom
problem.developer_concern: Did not want to create an unreliable workaround or charge the client for infrastructure that might not work

go_daddy_event.what_happened: During a support call, a GoDaddy representative sold the client a hosting package
go_daddy_event.result: Client now has both the domain and GoDaddy hosting
go_daddy_event.developer_decision: Rather than undoing the purchase, adapt the project architecture to use the GoDaddy hosting

core_architecture_lesson.hosting: The server/platform that serves the website
core_architecture_lesson.key_principle: Domain, hosting, and source code are separate layers
core_architecture_lesson.important_principle: Source code should remain independent from the hosting provider

recommended_architecture.ai_role: Development assistant, not owner of the project

netlify.status: Not necessarily needed for this project
netlify.lesson: Netlify and GoDaddy are hosting/deployment options rather than competing definitions of the project
netlify.future_use: Netlify can still be useful for future projects
netlify.principle: The same source code can potentially be deployed to different hosting platforms

git_github.reason: The website should not exist only inside Netlify, an AI builder, or a hosting account
git_github.desired_model: Local Git repository + GitHub remote repository

ai_philosophy.principle: AI should assist implementation rather than make architectural decisions autonomously
ai_philosophy.preferred_workflow: Decide what needs to be built, ask AI for implementation help or explanations, understand the generated code, test it, modify it, and commit it

learning_goal.main_goal: Develop a formal/repeatable web development workflow instead of relying on ad-hoc experimentation
learning_goal.secondary_goal: Learn enough web infrastructure to independently make architecture and deployment decisions
learning_goal.learning_style: Use AI to accelerate learning and implementation while retaining understanding and responsibility for the resulting system

important_context_for_future_ai.do_not_assume: The user is a beginner programmer overall
important_context_for_future_ai.instead_understand: The user has a solid CS foundation but is relatively inexperienced with professional web development and web infrastructure
important_context_for_future_ai.desired_role: The user wants to act as the developer, architect, and deployment administrator while using AI as a powerful assistant
important_context_for_future_ai.teaching_preference: Explain the underlying architecture and reasoning, not merely provide instructions
important_context_for_future_ai.current_learning_question: How to establish a professional, repeatable workflow for building, versioning, deploying, and maintaining client websites
